assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in V\) and assignments \(z,z'\in\{0,1\}^{n}\), \(z_{D_i}=z'_{D_i}\) implies \(Y_i(z)=Y_i(z')\).
The potential-outcome schedule \(Y\) is fixed before the random priority order and focal treatment allocation are drawn.

novel.justification: This checkable support condition is satisfied whenever the conflict graph has at least two nonempty connected components, as in multi-village or multi-community experiments, because sequential greedy isolation selects at least one vertex per component.

assumptions.condition: An endpoint vector \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R^{2n}\) is admissible when \(\vartheta^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}\vartheta\le B^{2}\).

novel.justification: The graph-Sobolev ellipsoid permits arbitrary level shifts along connected components while penalizing endpoint variation across conflict edges; it is a transparent sensitivity class for village-network outcomes, and binary or otherwise bounded endpoints fit after choosing a conservative radius.

definitions.name: WRI unit-isolation conflict graph
definitions.construction: \(C_G=(V,E_C)\), where \(\{i,j\}\in E_C\) if and only if \(i\ne j\) and \(D_i\cap D_j\ne\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Sequential weighted random isolation law
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\Omega\), \(P_{\ell}(\pi)=\prod_{r=1}^{n}h_{\ell,\pi_r}/\bigl(\sum_{s=r}^{n}h_{\ell,\pi_s}\bigr)\); scan \(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n\) and put a vertex in \(S_{\ell}(\pi)\) exactly when it has no previously selected neighbor in \(C_G\).

definitions.name: Balanced restricted difference in means
definitions.construction: Given \(S_{\ell}\) of size \(K_{\ell}\), draw \(T_{\ell}\) uniformly among its \(t(K_{\ell})\)-subsets, set \(U_{\ell}=S_{\ell}\setminus T_{\ell}\), expose every \(i\in T_{\ell}\) to \(\mathbf 1_{D_i}\) and every \(i\in U_{\ell}\) to \(\mathbf 0_{D_i}\), and compute \(\widehat\tau_{\ell}=e_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}\theta\).

definitions.name: One- and two-marked isolated-count polynomial
definitions.construction: \(F_{\ell,A}(z)=\mathbb E_{\ell}[z^{K_{\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A\subseteq S_{\ell}\}]\) for every \(A\subseteq V\) with \(|A|\le 2\).

definitions.name: Graph-Sobolev endpoint class
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_G(B)=\{\vartheta\in\mathbb R^{2n}:\vartheta^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}\vartheta\le B^{2}\}\), for every integer \(n\ge2\).

definitions.name: Three-state forest integration messages
definitions.construction: Root each tree and put \(f_v(x)=h_{\ell v}x^{h_{\ell v}-1}\). For each child \(u\) define \(J_u(z)=\int_0^1B_u(y,z)\,dy\), \(D_u(z)=\int_0^1(A_u(y,z)+B_u(y,z))\,dy\), and \(E_u(x,z)=J_u(z)+\int_0^xA_u(y,z)\,dy\). Then \(A_v(x,z)=zf_v(x)\prod_u(J_u(z)+\int_0^xC_u(y,z)\,dy)\), \(C_v(x,z)=f_v(x)\prod_uE_u(x,z)\), and \(B_v(x,z)=f_v(x)(\prod_uD_u(z)-\prod_uE_u(x,z))\), with unselected states suppressed at tagged vertices and root output \(\int_0^1(A_v+B_v)\,dx\).

definitions.name: Factorized separator priority/count handle
definitions.construction: Starting from a nice decomposition \(\mathcal T\), index each bag message by the relative order of active priorities, selected or unselected labels, higher-priority domination bits, the tag pattern, and a truncated \(z\)-count polynomial. Represent each order-chamber conditional density by an exact factorized arithmetic circuit over rational coefficients and bag-priority variables; seek an equivalence relation or circuit-normalization rule under which introduce, edge, forget-integration, join, and coefficient-extraction operations remain executable in size \(2^{O(w\log(w+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)\).

definitions.name: Finite-library ellipsoidal risk game
definitions.construction: Primal: \(\min_{q\in\Delta_L,t\in\mathbb R}B^{2}t\) subject to \(Q(q)\preceq tH^{-1}\). Dual: \(\max_{X\succeq0,s\in\mathbb R}B^{2}s\) subject to \(\operatorname{tr}(H^{-1}X)=1\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(Q_{\ell}X)\ge s\) for every \(\ell\).

definitions.name: Exact rational-input and real-algebraic-output encoding
definitions.construction: Encode every rational entry of \(B\), \(H\), and \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_L\) by a signed binary numerator and positive binary denominator. Encode each real-algebraic output coordinate by a square-free integer polynomial and a rational isolating interval; \(\Lambda\) denotes the total rational-input bit length.

definitions.name: Simultaneous Monte Carlo risk programs
definitions.construction: Draw \(a_{\ell1},\ldots,a_{\ell N}\) independently from rule \(\ell\), form \(\widehat Q_{\ell}=N^{-1}\sum_sa_{\ell s}a_{\ell s}^{\mathsf T}\), and define \(V_{-}\) and \(V_{+}\) by the minimax SDP with \(Q_{\ell}\) replaced by \(\widehat Q_{\ell}-\varepsilon I_{2n}\) and \(\widehat Q_{\ell}+\varepsilon I_{2n}\), respectively; let \(q_{+}\) minimize the upper program.

statements.statement: For every rule \(\ell\), the RDIM error is the \(2n\)-dimensional random linear form \(\widehat\tau_{\ell}-\tau=a_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}\theta\), and its exact design-based mean squared error is \(\mathbb E_{\ell}[(\widehat\tau_{\ell}-\tau)^2]=\theta^{\mathsf T}Q_{\ell}\theta\).
statements.justification: This exact quadratic object retains selection bias, random denominators, and randomization variance in one design-computable matrix.
statements.gap: Shi et al. bound RDIM MSE by a surrogate; they do not state the exact endpoint quadratic risk.
statements.consumer: The matrix is the loss input required to choose a prespecified WRI rule for a rural-China insurance-information follow-up.

statements.statement: For a strict priority order \(\pi\), a set \(S\subseteq V\) equals the sequential greedy output on \(C_G\) if and only if \(S\) is independent in \(C_G\) and every \(v\in V\setminus S\) has a neighbor \(u\in S\) that precedes \(v\) in \(\pi\).
statements.justification: The certificate converts a history-dependent greedy process into separator-local independence and domination constraints.
statements.gap: Random sequential adsorption studies the same process probabilistically, but the separator-local certificate is not developed there for marked exact integration.
statements.consumer: It is the logical invariant needed by both a tree-decomposition algorithm and a parameterized-hardness reduction.

statements.statement: Let \(p_{\ell i}(k)=[z^k]F_{\ell,\{i\}}(z)\) and \(p_{\ell ij}(k)=[z^k]F_{\ell,\{i,j\}}(z)\). Put \(m_{\ell}=(r_{\ell}^{\mathsf T},-r_{\ell}^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\), where \(r_{\ell i}=\sum_{k=2}^{n}p_{\ell i}(k)/k\), and \(M_{\ell}=\mathbb E_{\ell}[e_{\ell}e_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}]\). Then \(Q_{\ell}=M_{\ell}-m_{\ell}d^{\mathsf T}-dm_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}+dd^{\mathsf T}\). Its treated and control diagonal entries are \(\sum_kp_{\ell i}(k)/(kt(k))\) and \(\sum_kp_{\ell i}(k)/(kc(k))\); for \(i\ne j\), its corresponding blocks before centering are \(\sum_kp_{\ell ij}(k)(t(k)-1)/(t(k)k(k-1))\), \(\sum_kp_{\ell ij}(k)(c(k)-1)/(c(k)k(k-1))\), and \(-\sum_kp_{\ell ij}(k)/(k(k-1))\). Thus all entries of every \(Q_{\ell}\) are determined by tags of size at most two.
statements.justification: This is the sufficient-statistic reduction that makes exact dense risk a finite family of marked counting queries.
statements.gap: Neither AWRI nor randomized graph clustering retains the joint count law required by RDIM's reciprocal denominators and bias.
statements.consumer: An exact marked-moment oracle immediately produces every risk matrix used by the certified rule-mixture design.

statements.statement: For positive integer weights, every coefficient of \(F_{\ell,A}\) is rational with denominator dividing \((\sum_i h_{\ell i})!\), and every entry of \(Q_{\ell}\) has a common denominator dividing \((\sum_i h_{\ell i})!(n!)^3\). Numerators and denominators therefore have \(O(nb\log(nb+1)+n\log(n+1))\) bits.
statements.justification: The output-size bound separates a genuine running-time obstruction from exponential-length rational output.
statements.gap: Existing WRI work permits real weights and does not establish exact rational output or bit complexity.
statements.consumer: It permits auditable exact risk certificates for bounded-integer priority rules.

statements.statement: If \(C_G\) is a forest, the three-state forest-message construction computes every \(F_{\ell,A}\) exactly and hence every \(Q_{\ell}\) in \(L\operatorname{poly}(n,b)\) bit operations, uniformly over all \(|A|\le2\).
statements.justification: The forest theorem is a nontrivial solved rung and a falsifiable base case for any separator invariant.
statements.gap: Pippenger and Krivelevich et al. study occupancy or expected size on trees, not the complete weighted marked count law needed for exact causal risk.
statements.consumer: Village conflict forests receive an exact design selector even if the general fixed-parameter question is negative.

statements.statement: For binary-encoded rational inputs \(B>0\), \(H\succ0\), and \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_L\succeq0\), finite-dimensional semidefinite duality gives optimizers attaining \(V^{\star}=B^2t^{\star}=B^2s^{\star}\) at \((q^{\star},t^{\star})\) and \((X^{\star},s^{\star})\), including zero coordinates of \(q^{\star}\) and repeated leading generalized eigenspaces. If \(H^{-1/2}X^{\star}H^{-1/2}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\lambda_j u_ju_j^{\mathsf T}\), then \(\nu^{\star}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\lambda_j\delta_{BH^{1/2}u_j}\), with \(r\le2n\), is least favourable, and \(\operatorname{tr}(Q_{\ell}X^{\star})=s^{\star}\) whenever \(q_{\ell}^{\star}>0\). In the exact Turing model of the algebraic-certificate encoding, generic real quantifier elimination returns such real-algebraic optimizers in at most \((\Lambda Ln)^{2^{O(L+n^2)}}\) bit operations. Any rational feasible primal--dual pair certifies gap \(B^2(t-s)\).
statements.justification: This is a standard finite-SDP consequence of having exact rational risk matrices; it supplies the decision certificate but is not an independent novelty claim.
statements.gap: Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong provide the generic minimax semidefinite-design machinery; the proposition records its exact encoding and endpoint interpretation for the WRI library without claiming a new duality theorem.
statements.consumer: It converts any exact marked-moment oracle into a verifiable rule mixture before the rural-China insurance-information follow-up.

statements.statement: Establish one of two separator-boundary results. On the positive branch, using the factorized handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{sep}}\), output every \(F_{\ell,A}\) and every dense \(Q_{\ell}\) exactly from a width-\(w\) decomposition in \(Ln^2 2^{O(w\log(w+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)\) bit operations. Combined with the standard finite-SDP proposition, this branch returns \(q^{\star}\), \(\nu^{\star}\), and a primal--dual zero-gap certificate in total time \(Ln^2 2^{O(w\log(w+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)+(\Lambda Ln)^{2^{O(L+n^2)}}\). On the negative branch, establish \(\#\mathrm{W[1]}\)-hardness or \(\mathrm{W[1]}\)-hardness parameterized by \(w\) for one required one- or two-marked coefficient under positive weights bounded by \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\). Either branch settles the separator boundary for the prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count oracle. The positive-branch certificate concerns this restricted oracle and is neither an algorithm for nor a consequence of the unrestricted design-and-estimator maximal-independent-set functional.
statements.justification: This positive-versus-hard theorem-level target is the tier-bearing contribution: it resolves whether separator joins admit exact fixed-parameter integration and converts the positive resolution into an auditable minimax WRI design.
statements.gap: Kangas, Koivisto, and Salonen provide only an XP order-counting analogue. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje study an implicit unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax functional in Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10, but do not compute the prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count oracle or provide its fixed-parameter risk certificate.
statements.consumer: A positive branch supplies an explicit low-treewidth runtime and certified mixture for the rural-China insurance-information follow-up; a negative branch gives a parameterized reason to use the arbitrary-graph Monte Carlo certificate.

statements.statement: Let \(A_n^2=2-2/n\). If \(0<\varepsilon\le A_n^2\) and \(N\ge(8/3)A_n^4\varepsilon^{-2}\log(4nL/\delta)\), then \(\Pr\{\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat Q_{\ell}-Q_{\ell}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon\}\ge1-\delta\). On this event, \(V_{-}\le V^{\star}\le V_{+}\), the returned mixture satisfies \(\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta_G(B)}\vartheta^{\mathsf T}Q(q_{+})\vartheta\le V_{+}\), and \(V_{+}-V_{-}\le2B^2\varepsilon\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}=2B^2\varepsilon\).
statements.justification: This supplies a finite-sample fallback for arbitrary graphs while preserving the spectral loss relevant to the selected mixture.
statements.gap: Ugander and Yin resample exposure probabilities, and Tropp controls matrix sums; no located result gives a simultaneous exact-RDIM rule-matrix region with a downstream minimax-risk gap.
statements.consumer: The experimenter receives a risk certificate even when the observed village conflict graph has large treewidth.

statements.statement: If \(C_G\) has no edges, then \(S_{\ell}=V\) for every \(\ell\) and every priority order, all \(Q_{\ell}\) coincide, every mixture has the same risk, and \(\widehat\tau_{\ell}\) is the usual balanced complete-randomization difference in means for the finite-population total effect.
statements.justification: The reduction verifies that the proposed objects collapse to the classical no-interference design.
statements.gap: This is a required sanity reduction rather than an independent novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It lets practitioners interpret the method as a network-aware extension of standard complete randomization.

sampling_model.design: A graph-only draw of \(\ell\sim q\), followed by a weighted random-priority sequential greedy isolated set and balanced complete randomization over its focal units.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, directed graph, and full potential-outcome schedule are fixed; only the design is random.
sampling_model.treatment: For treated focal \(i\), all units in \(D_i\) receive treatment; for control focal \(i\), all units in \(D_i\) receive control; remaining assignments are fixed by the prespecified rule.
sampling_model.overlap: Every priority order under every library rule produces at least two isolated units, so both RDIM arms are nonempty.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Exact risk uses only the known graph and randomization law; the arbitrary-graph fallback uses independent offline design simulations, not field outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 bounds RDIM MSE using degree-distribution discrepancies and reciprocal isolated-arm sizes, and Section 4.2 minimizes a simulated surrogate.
Randomized graph clustering permits resampled exposure probabilities and exact randomized 3-net probability computation is hard on general graphs.
Counting linear extensions is not FPT in cover-graph treewidth unless \(\mathrm{W[1]}=\mathrm{FPT}\), but is FPT in incomparability-graph treewidth.
Counting linear extensions from a width-\(w\) cover-graph decomposition is possible in \(\widetilde O(n^{w+3})\) time using multivariate-polynomial joins.
Random sequential adsorption yields occupancy probabilities on regular and locally tree-like graphs.
Local-limit differential equations compute asymptotic random-greedy independent-set densities for broad graph sequences.
Semidefinite and nonlinear programming compute minimax optimal designs for semidefinite-representable criteria on discretized design spaces.
Matrix Bernstein bounds the maximum eigenvalue of a sum of independent centered bounded self-adjoint matrices.
Worst-case cluster-design MSE is optimized through a penalized min-cut and semidefinite relaxation under network interference.
The Conflict Graph Design attains a finite-sample variance bound of order \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) for a modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator.

Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10, analyze the unrestricted joint design-and-estimator minimax problem through an implicit functional involving distributions over maximal independent sets.

tldr: Weighted random isolation makes full-neighborhood treatment and control observable on a random independent set, but its restricted difference in means has random denominators and can be biased for the finite-population total effect. The core reduction writes this error as a \(2n\)-coordinate linear form and shows that every exact risk entry is determined by one- and two-marked isolated-count polynomials. The tier-bearing question is whether those polynomials admit an output-sensitive fixed-parameter algorithm in conflict-graph treewidth, yielding an explicit-runtime certified minimax mixture, or whether a required marked coefficient is parameterized-hard. A complete exact forest oracle supplies the positive base case. Exact rational matrices feed a standard finite-library ellipsoidal SDP consequence, while independent offline simulations give an operator-norm certificate on arbitrary graphs.

project_justification.gap: AWRI selects priority weights using an MSE surrogate, randomized graph clustering resorts to exposure-probability resampling on unrestricted graphs, and order-counting theory warns that bounded treewidth does not automatically make priority integration fixed-parameter tractable. The closest unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax analysis leaves its maximal-independent-set functional implicit and does not compute the prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count risk.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an exact, output-sensitive oracle for the marked isolated-count moments that determine dense RDIM risk, together with a positive-versus-hard separator frontier and an explicit certified-mixture guarantee on the positive branch.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact marked-moment reduction, establishes rational output and a complete forest base case, and asks for either fixed-parameter separator compression or parameter-preserving hardness. On the positive branch, standard semidefinite optimization converts the exact oracle into an exactly certified WRI mixture with a stated runtime; arbitrary graphs retain a simulation fallback.

related_work: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li supply the WRI/RDIM setup, directed full-neighborhood motivation, and surrogate-based weight-selection arc that informs the present setup. Ugander and Yin show how offline random graph-design draws can estimate otherwise intractable probabilities and establish a neighboring general-graph hardness boundary. Eiben, Ganian, Kangas, and Ordyniak show that the relevant order-counting intuition is representation-sensitive: cover-graph treewidth does not yield FPT linear-extension counting, whereas incomparability-treewidth does. Kangas, Koivisto, and Salonen handle cover-treewidth joins by multivariate polynomial multiplication with an exponent depending on width, the closest algorithmic analogue to the direct WRI messages. Pippenger and Krivelevich, Mészáros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman analyze random greedy occupancy and asymptotic size, but not exact weighted marked count distributions. Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong provide the standard minimax semidefinite-design machinery used only after causal risk matrices are available. Viviano et al. optimize cluster partitions under worst-case network MSE, while Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw study a different conflict-graph estimator. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje are the closest unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax and maximal-independent-set comparator: version 1, Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10, develops an implicit unrestricted functional, whereas the present theorem-level question concerns exact computation of a prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count functional and a certified restricted-library mixture. The unrestricted comparator informs scope; it is not claimed to be tightened or reproduced.
technical_internal_limitation: The direct nice-tree-decomposition construction stores piecewise multivariate priority polynomials with \(\binom{nb+w}{w}\) coefficients and therefore proves only XP complexity. Finite checks on widths two and three can falsify a proposed invariant but cannot establish FPT. The field-level contribution requires either a representation closed under exact joins and forget integrations with exponent independent of \(w\), followed by the stated certified-mixture runtime, or a parameter-preserving hardness reduction for a required marked coefficient. The standard finite-SDP consequence, the exact forest oracle, and matrix concentration do not by themselves settle this separator boundary.
honest_scope: The exact linear-risk reduction, rational-output bound, forest recurrence, standard finite-SDP consequence, and matrix-concentration fallback are all posed for proof, not treated as established by the presolve draft. The separator-compression versus parameterized-hardness dichotomy remains the genuine open content, and neither branch is asserted as proved. The finite-library minimax result concerns a prespecified WRI/RDIM oracle and does not claim equality with the unrestricted joint design-and-estimator minimax functional of Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje. Under an empty conflict graph the construction reduces to balanced complete randomization, providing the required classical sanity check.

seed_details.title: Exact marked-risk oracle: fixed-parameter compression or hardness
seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 3, Theorem 4.1, Appendix S2.1, and Section 6
seed_details.opened_evidence: Algorithm 3 defines the sequential weighted isolation law; Theorem 4.1 bounds RDIM risk by representativeness and reciprocal isolated-arm sizes; Appendix S2.1 supplies the surrogate proof; Section 6 identifies rigorous theory and computationally effective probability approximation as open.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace the surrogate by the exact dense quadratic risk and decide whether all one- and two-marked reciprocal-count moments admit an output-sensitive \(2^{O(w\log(w+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)\) oracle or are parameterized-hard.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At a tree-decomposition join, synchronize relative bag priorities, selected-versus-blocked labels, and the isolated-count generating variable without expanding \((nb)^{O(w)}\) monomials.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the exact target--method pair using random greedy maximal independent sets, marked moments, reciprocal counts, and treewidth found asymptotic occupancy results and an \(\widetilde O(n^{w+3})\) linear-extension analogue, but no WRI marked-risk oracle.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from ordinary bounded-treewidth dynamic programming because maximal independent sets are monadic-second-order definable.
seed_details.rebuttal: The design probability is a weighted measure over priority orders, not a count of independent sets; Eiben et al. show that order counting can remain non-FPT at bounded cover-graph treewidth, and the direct WRI polynomial messages have \((nb)^{O(w)}\) size.

seed_details.title: Parameterized hardness of a single marked WRI moment
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1 and Section 3, especially the equitable-coloring reduction and flower gadgets; Section 5
seed_details.opened_evidence: Theorem 1 rules out an FPT algorithm for counting linear extensions parameterized by cover-graph treewidth unless \(\mathrm{W[1]}=\mathrm{FPT}\); the proof encodes equitable coloring through congruences while controlling treewidth; the conclusion leaves finer counting classifications open.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Encode the order constraints of the source problem into the probability that one or two marked vertices survive sequential WRI while preserving the conflict-graph treewidth.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The poset flower gadget must be replaced by a domination gadget whose weighted priority-order probability is recoverable from a tagged isolated-set coefficient.
seed_details.destination_search: No parameter-preserving reduction to weighted random greedy isolation was located; the closest positive analogue is Kangas, Koivisto, and Salonen's XP tree-decomposition algorithm.
seed_details.red_team: Eiben et al.'s hardness already settles this because WRI also integrates priority orders.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their oracle counts linear extensions of a poset, while WRI accepts orders through a graph domination certificate; neither a parsimonious nor a Turing reduction preserving treewidth is available.
seed_details.disposition: dropped-after-ranking because the positive-or-negative dichotomy subsumes it

seed_details.title: Marked-moment characterization of exact RDIM risk
seed_details.opened_evidence: The paper targets the finite-population total effect and selects WRI weights by a degree-distribution and inverse-size surrogate rather than by the exact bias-plus-variance matrix.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Express RDIM error as a \(2n\)-coordinate random linear form and recover every risk entry from isolated-set count polynomials tagged by at most two vertices, retaining odd counts and random denominators.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Lipschitz surrogate inequality in the proof of Theorem 4.1 by conditional hypergeometric products and an exact expansion of \(\mathbb E[(e-d)(e-d)^{\mathsf T}]\).
seed_details.destination_search: Exact-title and formula searches found no paper deriving the full dense RDIM risk matrix for WRI.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a routine covariance expansion of the estimator in Shi et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: The expansion is a necessary but insufficient contribution; it survives only as the reduction that defines the nontrivial marked counting oracle.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a standalone seed and retained as Proposition 1

seed_details.title: Standard finite-SDP certificate for a prespecified WRI library
seed_details.opened_evidence: AWRI simulates a surrogate over candidate weights and selects one rule; it does not randomize across the library against exact ellipsoidal RDIM risk.
seed_details.proof_boundary: After exact rational rule risks are available, apply standard finite semidefinite duality under an explicit binary-input and real-algebraic-output encoding.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: No novel duality step is claimed; the substantive input is the exact matrix oracle, after which the epigraph constraint \(\sum_{\ell}q_{\ell}Q_{\ell}\preceq tH^{-1}\) yields the certificate.
seed_details.destination_search: Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong provide semidefinite minimax-design machinery, and Viviano et al. optimize cluster partitions, but neither result supplies exact WRI risks or the stated endpoint certificate.
seed_details.red_team: The minimax mixture is an immediate E-optimal design SDP.
seed_details.rebuttal: The SDP is standard once the risk matrices exist, so this seed is not tier-bearing and is retained only as a certified design consequence of the exact oracle.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a standalone seed and retained as a standard proposition downstream of the exact oracle

seed_details.title: Simultaneous operator-norm risk regions on arbitrary graphs
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 4.1.3, the exact-probability hardness result, Monte Carlo probability construction, and Section 7
seed_details.opened_evidence: Randomized graph clustering makes design-law quantities accessible through offline resampling even when exact exposure probabilities are hard, but its guarantees concern exposure probabilities and estimator variance rather than dense RDIM risk selection.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Construct independent self-adjoint per-draw risk contributions and propagate simultaneous matrix Bernstein regions through the mixture eigenvalue game.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Estimate \(aa^{\mathsf T}\) directly, rather than separately estimating marginal exposure probabilities, so random reciprocal counts and bias remain inside each draw.
seed_details.destination_search: Tropp's Theorem 1.4 supplies the matrix concentration step; no located network-design paper propagates simultaneous rule-matrix regions into a certified post-selection minimax gap.
seed_details.red_team: This follows immediately from matrix Bernstein and Weyl's inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection holds for the generic concentration branch, so it is retained only as an arbitrary-graph fallback and not as the proposal kernel.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a standalone seed and retained as Theorem 7

seed_details.title: Studentized design-based RDIM limit after graph-only rule mixing
seed_details.opened_evidence: The consistency discussion is simulation-based and the conclusion explicitly requests more rigorous finite-population theory; no studentized RDIM limit law is supplied.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Derive uniform stabilization of the random isolated-set denominators and a conditional-to-unconditional CLT over a finite graph-only rule library.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Unlike a fixed exposure-indicator dependency graph, WRI first generates a random greedy support whose membership can depend on distant priority changes; the proof must localize or martingale-decompose this support before studentization.
seed_details.destination_search: Gao and Ding and Kandiros et al. provide design-based covariance and coverage for different exposure estimators; Chin provides dependency-graph Stein bounds; none treats RDIM's random greedy support and reciprocal denominators.
seed_details.red_team: Condition on the isolated set and apply the complete-randomization central limit theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Unconditioning adds random support, representativeness bias, and unstable reciprocal denominators; uniform control over graph-only rule selection is not supplied by a conditional theorem.

seed_details.title: Robust WRI risk over plausible interference graphs
seed_details.anchor_location: Setup assumption that the network is fixed and known, and Section 6 discussion of noisy or unobserved networks
seed_details.opened_evidence: The design is conditional on one known directed graph, while the conclusion identifies weighted, noisy, and unobserved social networks as a substantive limitation.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Optimize WRI risk over a compactly represented family of graph completions without enumerating all edge augmentations.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Graph-specific isolation must become a joint state over selected vertices and unresolved candidate edges because every completion changes the conflict graph and its risk law.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest robust-network papers average or bound across plausible networks but do not compute exact finite-population WRI risk; no compact separation oracle for this design class was located.
seed_details.red_team: Take the maximum of the fixed-graph risk matrices already computed for each candidate graph.
seed_details.rebuttal: That requires enumerating exponentially many completions and does not address the joint isolation-law change; the current substrate does not yet yield a credible compact oracle.

seed_details.title: Unrestricted minimax comparator boundary
seed_details.anchor_location: Version 1, Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10
seed_details.opened_evidence: Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10, analyze the unrestricted joint design-and-estimator minimax problem using an implicit functional involving distributions over maximal independent sets. They do not specify the prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count functional or an exact bounded-treewidth oracle for it.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Use the unrestricted result only as the closest scope comparator. The proposal targets exact marked-moment computation and certified mixing within a prespecified WRI/RDIM library, not equality with or computation of the unrestricted functional.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The separator algorithm must integrate weighted priority orders and reciprocal isolated counts for fixed RDIM rules; no optimizer or estimand from the unrestricted design-and-estimator problem is assumed.
seed_details.destination_search: The unrestricted minimax manuscript supplies no exact algorithm for the WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count oracle; finite optimal-design duality applies only after those restricted risk matrices have been computed.
seed_details.red_team: The unrestricted minimax maximal-independent-set formulation already yields the proposed exact risk oracle and mixture.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its design-and-estimator functional is implicit and unrestricted, whereas the proposed oracle must output each dense RDIM matrix for a prespecified weighted-priority rule, including one- and two-marked reciprocal-count moments.
seed_details.disposition: retained only as the closest unrestricted comparator, not as a claimed frontier theorem

literature_map.settled: Sequential weighted isolation on directed networks, RDIM, a degree-balance and inverse-size MSE surrogate, and simulation-based rule choice.
literature_map.open_boundary: Exact dense finite-population RDIM risk and tractable marked reciprocal-count moments are not supplied.

literature_map.thread: Randomized graph constructions and exact probability hardness
literature_map.settled: Randomized 3-net and one-hop-max clustering, offline resampling of exposure probabilities, polynomial variance bounds under graph growth restrictions, and general-graph hardness for an exact randomized 3-net probability.
literature_map.open_boundary: The result neither studies WRI's sequential greedy conflict graph nor returns one- and two-marked isolated-set count polynomials.
literature_map.used_as: Method exemplar for separating offline design draws from the field assignment.

literature_map.settled: Counting linear extensions is not FPT in cover-graph treewidth unless \(\mathrm{W[1]}=\mathrm{FPT}\), is FPT in incomparability-graph treewidth, and admits an \(\widetilde O(n^{w+3})\) cover-graph algorithm using multivariate-polynomial joins.
literature_map.open_boundary: No reduction transfers the hardness to WRI marked moments, and no positive result compresses WRI priority/count messages to FPT size.
literature_map.used_as: Method exemplar for both the obstruction test and the join-state architecture.

literature_map.settled: Occupancy probabilities, asymptotic greedy independence ratios, local-limit differential equations, and exact extremal expected-size results for trees.
literature_map.open_boundary: These papers do not compute finite-graph weighted tagged count distributions, reciprocal counts, or dense causal risk matrices.
literature_map.used_as: Adjacent probability thread confirming that the exact target--method pair is unoccupied.

literature_map.settled: A modified Horvitz--Thompson conflict-graph design has spectral risk-rate guarantees. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje version 1, Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10, analyze an unrestricted joint design-and-estimator minimax functional involving maximal independent sets.
literature_map.open_boundary: The unrestricted functional is implicit and distinct from the prespecified weighted-WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count oracle; neither paper computes its dense rule risks or gives a bounded-treewidth priority-order algorithm.
literature_map.used_as: Closest unrestricted scope comparator, explicitly not a claimed tightening.
